The *Khantivaṇṇajātaka* (Ja 225) is a narrative included in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. According to the traditional introductory narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha recounted the story at Jetavana regarding the King of Kosala. A highly competent subordinate in the royal service had engaged in an intrigue within the king's harem; nevertheless, acknowledging the official's usefulness, the king chose to bear the insult with forbearance and reported the situation to the Buddha. In response, the Buddha noted that rulers in ancient times had acted likewise and narrated the tale of the past (*atītavatthu*).
